title: Chanina Yaot
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: So he is listed in Seder HaDorot, citing Demai 3:4. The rabbi known as Maskil LeEitan already criticized this: the word yaot belongs to what follows. In fact, the passage refers to Rabbi Chanina, the rabbis' colleague.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Yaot is “properly” or “well,” not part of the name in Hyman’s correction. חברון דרבנן means the rabbis’ colleague, not a place or personal name Hebron. The consulted Demai passage places yaot after the preceding clause.

The checked Demai 3:4 text contains the sequence ולא עאל יאות הוה רבי חנינא. It does not itself supply the phrase ‘the rabbis’ colleague’ in that passage. That explanation, the attribution to Maskil LeEitan, and the account of Seder HaDorot remain Hyman’s reports; the relevant bibliographic notices have not been directly collated. The existing note is retained alongside this qualification.
